title: cross-runner traffic sharder and latency-path linker
author: Maya Chen

description: Summary: Introduces a traffic sharder for synthetic benchmark runners that can partition generated requests across multiple runner instances (shards) and a latency-path linker reporter that correlates end-to-end latency across shard boundaries. Motivation: Existing runners model single-process hotspots and interleaved sequences but do not easily emulate cross-runner contention and backpressure that customers see with multi-pod deployments. This makes it hard to reproduce p95/p99 regressions caused by shard-local queuing and cross-shard coordination. Solution: Add a pluggable sharder component that sits in the workload generator and shards traffic according to configurable policies (hash-by-session, round-robin windowed, adaptive hotset split). Each request is stamped with a lightweight correlation id and a path tag so the latency-path linker can stitch traces across shards and produce per-path p50/p95/p99 deltas as well as a per-shard affinity heatmap export. Implementation notes: Python prototype for the sharder lives in runners/sharder.py and provides a local simulation harness; the latency-path linker reporter is implemented in Go to integrate with existing reporter pipelines and emits a compact CSV and Prometheus-friendly metrics via shard_affinity_exporter.py. We also added a small C++ worker hotpath fix for multi-threaded enqueue semantics in shard_worker_impl.cc and a convenience CLI + Dockerfile to run a small multi-shard cluster locally. Tests and verification: integration test simulates 3 shard topologies and asserts deterministic trace stitching and bucketed latency deltas (tests/integration/test_cross_shard_replay.py). Performance runs were executed in the perf pipeline (ci/perf-pipeline-config.yaml) with a synthetic workload manifest (benchmarks/manifests/cross-shard-sim.yaml). Results: baseline run (3 shards, hash-by-session) shows expected p95 uplift of ~18% when hotset affinity is enabled vs evenly distributed baseline; exporter produces per-shard heatmap and CSV with path-linked histograms. Commits: initial + linker + exporter + tuning + race fix + docs. Review conversation summary: Reviewer Anika requested CLI knobs for shard window size and a short reproducible example; addressed in commit 4 and added examples/cross_shard_quickstart.md. Liam pointed out a potential memory growth in the correlation map; fixed by using a bounded LRU in shard_affinity_exporter.py and added tests. Diego requested clearer labels for exported metrics and a Prometheus exposition check — added labels and unit test. CI: lint, unit, integration and perf checks ran; the perf pipeline first run flagged a transient worker-race (investigated and resolved) then all checks passed on rerun. Merge: merged into main via squash. Release notes: Adds a sharder and latency linking reporter to the benchmark lab to help reproduce cross-pod contention, export per-shard affinity heatmaps and path-linked latency deltas; recommended for multi-pod performance investigations. Follow-ups: add a scale test for >16 shard topologies and integrate the linker with the evaluation harness to automatically compare model variants under sharded traffic patterns.
